trainers.instruction: Select the falcon-headed god in the image.

hint.label: Falcon
text: A falcon is a bird of prey.

feedback.correct: This is Ra, one of the most important Egyptian gods.

atoms.b: The ancient Egyptian Sun god was called Ra. According to legend, he would carry the Sun ((++across under)) the sky from east to west in his boat every day.
Ra is often shown with a ((++falcon’s_head horse’s_head)). Ra was also thought to be the ((grandmother ++father)) of all the pharaohs.

feedback.finish: Ra’s journey across the sky helped the Egyptians explain the cycle of day and night. At night, Ra was said to be journeying through the underworld!

b: Ra was known for his ability to build beautiful pyramids.
++Ra rode a boat across the sky every day.
++Ra was considered the father of all pharaohs.

hint.label: Jackal
text: A jackal is a wolf-like animal found in Africa.

correct.text: This is Anubis, the god of mummification and guardian of the dead.
correct.sound: This is Anoobis, the god of mummification and guardian of the dead.

atoms.b: Anubis is usually shown with the head of a ((++dog sheep)) or a jackal. He has pointed ears and wears a colourful ribbon around his neck.
atoms.sound: Anoobis is usually shown with the head of a dog or a jackal. He has pointed ears and wears a colourful ribbon around his neck.

atoms.b: Anubis was the protector and judge of the ((++dead children)). He led the deceased to the underworld.
atoms.sound: Anoobis was the protector and judge of the dead. He led the deceased to the underworld.

atoms.b: People were judged by having their heart placed on a ((++scale oven)) and weighed against a feather. The more ((++sinful seasick)) a heart was, the heavier it would be.

finish.text: Anubis was the main judge of the dead, but he was helped by 42 other gods! Each god represented a specific sin.
finish.sound: Anoobis was the main judge of the dead, but he was helped by 42 other gods! Each god represented a specific sin.

instruction.text: This scene shows Anubis judging a person. Drag the heart to its correct place on the scales.
What do you think will happen to this person?

text.text: If your heart was heavier than the feather, you failed the test, and your soul would have been eaten by a terrifying monster!

instruction.text: Drag this other person’s heart to the scales.
What do you think will happen to this person?

text.text: Those who passed the test would be allowed to pass into the afterlife and live alongside Osiris, the god of the underworld.
